newsitem.title: USA: U2 tour in United States fails to live up to hype. [CORRECTED 02:00 GMT 6/6]
newsitem.headline: U2 tour in United States fails to live up to hype. [CORRECTED 02:00 GMT 6/6]

text.p: Irish rock band U2's ambitious "PopMart" stadium tour appears to have fallen short of its hype with at least two shows already cancelled, possibly due to slow ticket sales.

"About 20 percent of the dates have been less than overwhelming," Paul Wasserman, U2's publicist in Los Angeles said on Thursday. "One hopes for total capacity everywhere but that doesn't always happen."

The band, touring to promote its latest album "Pop", has cancelled a concert in Philadelphia scheduled for Saturday. Wasserman said the move was due to a scheduling conflict with a Tibetan Freedom Concert in New York but others claim slow ticket sales were behind the change of plans.

Ticketholders who had bought seats for the cancelled show were told as early as last week that the performance was being cancelled due to weak ticket sales. However, a Philadelphia show scheduled for Sunday will proceed as planned (clarifies that Sunday concert is taking place).
"I don't believe any of the shows have been sold out," said one source at a major ticket outlet.
The tour kicked off in Las Vegas on April 25 to mixed reviews. The band was scheduled to play 44 concerts in North America including the second leg of the tour which kicks off in October.

At least two of the shows, in Denver and San Diego, were only about half full. According to the Denver Post the band's show in Mile High Stadium on May 1 only attracted 27,000 fans to the venue with a capacity of about 60,000. Four (corrects from two) years ago, 53,000 fans went to Mile High stadium to hear the band play.

Susan Rosenberg of the tour's promotion company Step Entertainment Services, denied the Philadelphia show was nixed as a result of flacid sales adding the shows in San Diego and Denver "were over half full as a matter of fact."
"We consider ticket sales very strong," she said, declining to give details.

Another date, in Raleigh, North Carolina, on May 29 was also cancelled. Promoters said that show was called off due to damage done to the stage's LED VideoWall during a downpour before a show in Washington, D.C.
The tour is one of the biggest ever staged and reportedly costs $1.5 million a week to keep on the road. Promoters have said the world tour, over 100 shows, could gross about $400 million.
